newsitem.title: USA: Fed, SEC to host TV program on saving, investing.
newsitem.headline: Fed, SEC to host TV program on saving, investing.

text.p: The Federal Reserve and the Securities and Exchange Commission announced Friday they are co-sponsoring an educational television program designed to encourage adults to save and educate them about investing.
The program, "entitled "It's Your Money," will be broadcast nationwide by satellite on Nov. 9 at 11 a.m. Central time. It will be available via a variety of special outlets.

The hour-long seminar -- which will feature Fed Vice Chairwoman Alice Rivlin and SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt -- will cover the basics of saving and investing as well as look at "smart" ways to deal with today's markets.

Topics will include how to budget for savings, the use of compounding to help savings grow, and making investment choices. "It's a big mystery why Americans don't save more," Rivlin told a press conference in announcing the show.
"If we had a higher savings rate generally in the United States going forward, we would have a higher future standard of living," she added.

The program will be broadcast from Westcott Communications in Dallas and made available to individuals and groups through Westcott's Intercactive Distance Training Network and its affilates throughout the country.
The show will be made available to the Community College Satellite Network.

Members of the National University Teleconference Network also will have access to the teleseminar. American Financial Skylink, a unit of the American Bankers Association, will make the show available to subscribers in live format on Nov. 9, and in videotape format as a special program in December.
